observations.statement: If a polynomial-size d-DNNF with auxiliary variables projects exactly to a function, then forgetting the auxiliaries yields a polynomial-size ordinary DNNF for that function.
observations.support: Replace forgotten-variable literals by true and simplify. Decomposability is preserved and circuit size does not increase.

observations.statement: Auxiliary variables can bypass deterministic d-DNNF lower bounds without bypassing lower bounds against all DNNFs.
observations.support: Forgetting can destroy determinism but preserves ordinary DNNF, which is exactly why the H016 projection argument remains decisive.

observations.statement: A witness-recovery condition quantified only over accepting paths is vacuous unless the statement separately guarantees that satisfiable inputs have accepting paths and unsatisfiable inputs do not.
observations.support: An algorithm with no accepting paths satisfies the one-way witness condition vacuously.

observations.statement: A finite bounded-radius rule language is not automatically weaker than general polynomial-time computation; local transition systems can be computationally universal.
observations.support: Local syntax and constant-size transition checks do not by themselves establish a preserved structural invariant or rule out simulation of a polynomial-time machine.

observations.statement: The strongest located extension-variable lower bounds do not yet settle H010 because their field, dependency, or resource restrictions differ from recursively composed fan-in-two extensions over GF(2).
observations.support: R025 bounds finite-field extensions with bounded dependence on original variables; R026 proves a bit-size lower bound over the rationals.

observations.statement: The registry must support append-only tombstones: a later decisive attack may retire an entry while preserving its original cycle file, attacks, references, and descendants.
observations.support: Cycle C004 introduces terminal shadowing in the validator instead of rewriting historical snapshots.
